operations_plan.summary: Identify the sharp exterior edges on the left lateral side of the enlarged rear body and establish the corresponding opposite-side fillets as geometric references.

steps.description: Establish the part orientation and symmetry reference. Treat the longitudinal shank direction as X and the lateral direction as Y. Based on the semantic orientation, interpret the requested left side as the +Y side, but confirm this interpretation by locating the side of the enlarged rear body that contains sharp exterior edges opposite existing rounded edges. Construct or retrieve the longitudinal XZ center plane midway between the two lateral sides. If the semantic +Y designation conflicts with the geometry, use the visibly unfilleted side as the target because the wording 'left side' is otherwise unresolved by the request.

Inspect the enlarged rear body on both sides of the center plane and pair each sharp target-side exterior edge with its reflected edge on the already rounded side. Use the intersections and transitions involving the enlarged-body side walls, top face, bottom face, rear end wall, and shank shoulder to establish the edge correspondence. Since explicit B-rep edge IDs are unavailable, resolve the target edges by adjacency to faces 26 or 31 on the unfilleted side and faces 10, 34, 32, and 13 around its perimeter. Do not include internal edges or edges belonging to the bore or rectangular pocket.

Measure the existing opposite-side fillet geometry rather than assigning an arbitrary radius. Classify the reference rounds into the major 30 mm perimeter treatment represented by cylindrical faces 27, 28, 36, and 37 and spherical face 33, and the smaller 5 mm shoulder or edge treatment represented by cylindrical faces 23, 29, and 35 and spherical face 30. Use BSpline transition faces 21 and 22 to determine the required corner continuity and termination behavior. Record which sharp reflected edge receives the 30 mm radius and which receives the 5 mm radius.

operations_plan.summary: Add the matching 30 mm major perimeter fillets to the sharp left-side edges of the enlarged rear body.

steps.description: Select only the sharp major exterior edges on the target lateral side of the enlarged rear body that correspond, by reflection across the established XZ center plane, to the existing 30 mm rounded perimeter edges. These are the applicable enlarged-body edges between the target side wall and the rear and lower exterior surfaces. Exclude any edge without a rounded opposite-side counterpart and stop the selection at the shoulder where the enlarged body transitions into the narrower shank.

Apply constant-radius edge fillets of 30 mm to the selected major edges. Match the opposite-side fillet extent, setback, and rolling-ball transition behavior represented by faces 27, 28, 36, 37, and 33. Use tangent propagation only where the reflected reference fillet propagates across the same continuous edge chain; otherwise limit the fillet explicitly at the same reflected vertices or shoulder boundaries. The operation must remove material without enlarging the original external envelope.

Resolve intersections between the new 30 mm rounds as a three-edge corner blend equivalent to the opposite-side spherical or blended corner treatment. Match the topology and tangency of reference spherical face 33 and, where applicable, transition BSpline face 21. Confirm that no sliver faces, self-intersections, or unintended propagation into the shank are produced.

operations_plan.summary: Add the matching 5 mm secondary fillets at the left-side shoulder and remaining corresponding enlarged-body edges.

steps.description: After completion of the major rounds, select the remaining sharp target-side edges of the enlarged rear body that reflect the existing 5 mm edge treatment. Concentrate on the shoulder at the x=100 mm enlarged-body-to-shank junction and any adjacent lower or transverse edge having a 5 mm rounded counterpart. Use the target-side portion of shoulder face 13 and its adjacency to the enlarged side and bottom surfaces to locate these edges. Do not select the long edges of the narrow shank unless required to terminate the matching shoulder fillet continuously.

Apply constant-radius 5 mm fillets to the selected secondary edges, matching the radius and longitudinal or transverse extent of reference faces 23, 29, and 35. Terminate each new fillet at the same reflected limits as its opposite-side reference, preserving the narrower shank cross-section, the shoulder location, and the overall length of the part.

Create or allow the fillet solver to generate the target-side three-edge corner transition corresponding to spherical face 30 and blended face 22. Require tangent continuity between the new 5 mm shoulder rounds, the existing or newly created 30 mm perimeter rounds, and the adjacent planar faces. Compare the transition against the reflected opposite-side geometry and adjust only fillet ordering or corner setback if required to reproduce the same topology.

operations_plan.summary: Validate bilateral consistency of the enlarged-body radii and verify preservation of all functional interfaces.

steps.description: Reflect or compare the completed target-side enlarged-body boundary across the established XZ center plane against the original rounded opposite side. Verify equal 30 mm major radii, equal 5 mm secondary radii, matching edge-chain extents, equivalent corner transitions, and tangent continuity. Confirm that every newly rounded edge has a corresponding opposite-side reference and that no unrelated sharp edge was modified.

Run solid-validity and interference checks. Preserve the main shank geometry, front face, longitudinal blind bore, rectangular side pocket, and all existing opposite-side rounds. Specifically verify that bore faces 20 and 24 and pocket faces 5 and 15 through 19 are unchanged in size, position, orientation, and connectivity, and that the result remains one watertight solid.
